scope.fixed_last_matching: Exact necessary and sufficient capacity criterion for required-set forward reachability through a preceding matching, assuming each required set contains its own wire.
scope.adjacent_last_matching: Exact decision and construction of two matching layers whose forward cones contain a given vector of contiguous required intervals, with the last matching adjacent.
not_claimed: Sorting the full input data family
Replacing an arbitrary feasible last matching by an adjacent one while preserving preceding-matching feasibility

proof_review: A demanding wire must be partnered into its unique other last-layer block; every nonfree such partner must make the reciprocal demand.
Maximum reciprocal cancellation leaves exactly the stated excess incoming demand, which must fit the destination block free vertices.
Greedy reciprocal cancellation and injection into free vertices use disjoint source and destination sets and construct a valid preceding matching.
For adjacent blocks, interval containment and the capacity inequality depend only on the previous, current, and next blocks.
implementation_review: Endpoint buckets process states in topological order because every appended block advances the endpoint.
One predecessor per ordered pair of consecutive blocks is sufficient: older blocks have already passed their checks and no future check depends on earlier history.
Initial missing-left and final missing-right neighbors are handled explicitly, including one- and two-wire inputs.
Accepted tilings are reconstructed once by predecessor links; no copied recursive suffixes remain.
Each endpoint has at most four nonboundary states with at most two outgoing transitions; every local block has size at most two.
After acceptance every required interval lies in at most two adjacent blocks and has length at most four, so demand reconstruction is linear.
Greedy reciprocal cancellation constructs the preceding matching; array buckets indexed by the lower endpoint order its edges without a global comparison sort.
complexity: O(n) time and storage under the standard constant-time indexed/dictionary operation model, including reconstruction and edge ordering.

verification_evidence.action_this_review: Source and proof inspection; checked current verification report hashes against the reviewed algorithm and checker. No solver or additional test replay launched.
verification_evidence.checks_are: Corroboration of the proof, not a finite enumeration premise.
